title: extcap: Add extcap information and bookmark support
description:
Add an "extcap_info.json" file at the top of the personal configuration
directory that can contain arbitrary information about extcap
interfaces.
    
Use it to add support for extcap bookmarks, which lets you create
aliases / pseudo interfaces for a given extcap. For example, the 
bookmark "sshdump/My Cheap Router" represents an alias for "sshdump"
that shows up as a separate interface in Wireshark's main window and in
`tshark -D`.
    
Structure extcap_info.json to allow other per-extcap and per-interface
properties so that we can cache other information in the future.
    
Assisted-by: Claude
Fixes #14224

Getting the DLTs in parallel (2b14f0f806edfbf3cb9580767c5e3e299a63dd11) like the configurations mitigates this, but it's potentially wasteful to spawn multiple processes with the same "plain" extcap interface retrieving the same information. The config is tied into creating the preferences though, so it might take some work to separate it.

It might make sense to cache the results of extcap-config and perhaps extcap-dlt for a plain interface anyway. #15779 requests that but also gives an example with dynamic results. Caching something with dynamic results is tricky - we probably could cache until the interfaces are freed.

All that is worse on Windows where spawning processes is just orders of magnitude more expensive.

I think main_application.cpp has a line to reread the extcap preferences from the new profile when changing configuration profiles that probably shouldn't be needed now. I think - it's possible that the "no extcaps" preference changes but I think that gets picked up via other methods.

According to Claude, `setConfigurationProfile()` calls `prefs_reset()` via `readConfigurationProfiles()`. `extcap_register_preferences()`  doesn't subsequently restore extcap prefs because `_loaded_interfaces` is set, which prevents `extcap_register_preferences()` → `extcap_ensure_all_interfaces_loaded()` from reading extcap prefs.

This should be fixed now by exposing and calling `extcap_read_preferences()`.

Should the second parameter be `false` here now, to write this to the top level directory instead? (Maybe it's still true for backwards compatibility, but will this write prefs for bookmarks now that 4.4 and 4.6 won't understand?) Should this even be written here, or should it written in a different place? Right now the Extcap Options Dialog sends a PreferencesChanged signal which saves all the preferences saved (both extcaps and not), and we also save the extcap preferences incidentally at other times, which makes things complicated because we want to avoid overwriting extcap.cfg just because we're not loading the extcaps due to that capture preference.

If we can only write the extcap preferences when they change, i.e. from the extcap dialog, we can really simplify some of the extcap preference handling and try to move towards the InterfaceListManager being the sole instigator of total extcap interface scans. Right now there's some cases where the InterfaceListManager frees the extcap configuration even though some other part of the program just got done scanning them in order to load the extcap preferences.
Makes sense to me, since capture preferences (including extcap preferences) should IMHO be independent of our analysis preferences (i.e., anything we save to a profile).
